stem.en: Kabir says: "If the helix must be the same width, why not use only A-T pairs? Simpler." What does one kind of pair cost?

text.en: Information. A helix of only A-T pairs is a tape of two letters, which spells far less per position than four. And the extra strength of G-C is lost everywhere.

feedback.en: Fewer kinds of letter means fewer possible messages, from IV.7's counting. Four kinds is not decoration.
An all-A-T helix holds together, just less firmly. The real cost is what it can say.
A-T is one big and one small, the right width. Width is not the problem; alphabet size is.

explanation.en: The width rule allows exactly two pairs. Using both gives four letters and two strengths. Using one gives a thinner alphabet for no gain.
